title: Normalized homology injectivity descends by lifting the target boundary
statement: Let $X,Y$ be simplicial abelian groups and $f:X\to Y$ an additive simplicial morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For a simplicial set $S$, let $F(S)_m=\mathbb Z[S_m]$, the free abelian group with basis vectors $[s]$ indexed by $s\in S_m$; every simplicial operator acts by $[s]\mapsto[S(\varphi)(s)]$. For a simplicial-set map $a:S\to T$ put $F(a)_m([s])=[a_m(s)]$. Write $UZ$ for the underlying simplicial set of a simplicial abelian group $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $\epsilon_Z:F(UZ)\to Z$ be evaluation, given degreewise by $\sum_j a_j[z_j]\mapsto\sum_j a_jz_j$. For a simplicial abelian group $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], set $N(Z)_0=Z_0$ and $N(Z)_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\ker(d_i:Z_m\to Z_{m-1})$ for $m>0$, with differential $\partial_m=d_0$ for $m>0$ and $\partial_0=0$. Write $H_m(N(Z))=\ker\partial_m/\operatorname{im}\partial_{m+1}$; a simplicial morphism $a$ induces the chain map $N(a)$ by restriction in every degree. For every $n\geq0$, cycle $x\in N(X)_n$, and $y\in N(Y)_{n+1}$ with $d_0y=f_n(x)$, the elements $\widetilde x=[x]-[0_n]$ and $\widetilde y=[y]-[0_{n+1}]$ satisfy $\widetilde x\in N(F(UX))_n$ and $\partial_n\widetilde x=0$, $\widetilde y\in N(F(UY))_{n+1}$, $\partial_{n+1}\widetilde y=F(Uf)_n(\widetilde x)$, and $\epsilon_X(\widetilde x)=x$; when $n=0$ the cycle condition means the kernel of the zero differential, with no term in degree $-1$. Here $0_m$ is the zero simplex in degree $m$. Consequently, for every fixed $n\geq0$, if $H_n(N(F(Uf)))$ is injective then $H_n(N(f))$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), third proof paragraph, lines 5935-5958: lifting a kernel cycle and its target boundary, and injectivity transfer, in the higher-face normalization with differential d_0.

proof.text: First check the maps used below directly. For every simplicial operator $\varphi$ and generator $[z]$, both $Z(\varphi)\epsilon_Z([z])$ and $\epsilon_ZF(UZ)(\varphi)([z])$ equal $Z(\varphi)(z)$; additivity extends this equality to every finite sum. Thus evaluation commutes with faces. Likewise $F(Uf)$ commutes with faces since $f$ does [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], and $f\epsilon_X([z])=f(z)=\epsilon_YF(Uf)([z])$. Every such additive map preserves the intersections of face kernels and commutes with $d_0$, hence restricts to the indicated normalized chain map. The normalization itself is a complex: for $z\in N(Z)_m$ and $1\leq i\leq m-1$, the simplicial face identity gives $d_i d_0z=d_0d_{i+1}z=0$, and for $m\geq2$, $d_0d_0z=d_0d_1z=0$. These identities follow by composing the injections omitting the indicated vertices in $\Delta$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. In degree one the next differential is zero by definition.

source.place: Tag 08P2, lemma-homotopy-equivalence, injectivity paragraph (lines 5935–5958); generator argument written with higher-face normalization and differential d_0.

proof.text: For the specified cycle $x$, if $n>0$ then every face of $x$ is zero: the higher ones vanish by membership in $N(X)_n$ and $d_0x=0$ by the cycle condition. Since each face is additive, $d_i0_n=0_{n-1}$, so $d_i([x]-[0_n])=[d_ix]-[0_{n-1}]=0$ for every $0\leq i\leq n$. Thus $\widetilde x$ is normalized and is a cycle. If $n=0$, normalization imposes no equations and $\partial_0=0$, giving the same conclusion without a face to degree $-1$. Evaluation gives $\epsilon_X(\widetilde x)=x-0_n=x$. For $1\leq i\leq n+1$, similarly $d_i\widetilde y=[0_n]-[0_n]=0$. Finally $d_0\widetilde y=[d_0y]-[0_n]=[f_n(x)]-[0_n]=F(Uf)_n(\widetilde x)$, since $f_n(0_n)=0_n$. This proves every asserted lift formula.

source.place: Tag 08P2, lemma-homotopy-equivalence, injectivity paragraph (lines 5935–5958); generator argument written with higher-face normalization and differential d_0.

proof.text: Now fix $n$ and assume $H_n(N(F(Uf)))$ injective. Let $\xi$ lie in the kernel of $H_n(N(f))$. By the stated quotient definition write $\xi$ as the class of a cycle $x\in N(X)_n$. That its image is zero means exactly $f_n(x)\in\operatorname{im}\partial_{n+1}$, so choose $y\in N(Y)_{n+1}$ with $d_0y=f_n(x)$. Step 2 supplies the cycle $\widetilde x$ and the normalized element $\widetilde y$ with $F(Uf)_n(\widetilde x)=\partial_{n+1}\widetilde y$. Therefore the class of $\widetilde x$ maps to zero. Injectivity makes its class zero, which by the same quotient definition supplies $u\in N(F(UX))_{n+1}$ with $\partial_{n+1}u=\widetilde x$. These statements use only membership in the image subgroup, not any exactness theorem.

source.place: Tag 08P2, lemma-homotopy-equivalence, injectivity paragraph (lines 5935–5958); generator argument written with higher-face normalization and differential d_0.

proof.text: Put $v=\epsilon_{X,n+1}(u)$. To see explicitly that $v$ is normalized, write $u=\sum_j a_j[z_j]$. For each $1\leq i\leq n+1$, $d_iv=\sum_j a_jd_iz_j=\epsilon_{X,n}(d_iu)=0$ because $u$ is normalized. The same finite-sum calculation for $i=0$ yields $d_0v=\epsilon_{X,n}(d_0u)=\epsilon_{X,n}(\widetilde x)=x$. Thus $x$ is a boundary and $\xi=0$. This also works for $n=0$: only faces out of degree one occur. Hence the kernel of $H_n(N(f))$ is zero. If two homology classes have the same image, their difference lies in that kernel, so they are equal; this is the claimed injectivity.
